title: Build by Inserting at Given Slots
statement:
You get two arrays of equal length, nums and slots. Start with an empty list and process i = 0, 1, 2, … in order: insert nums[i] so that it ends up at index slots[i], shifting everything at that index and after it one place to the right.

Every insert is valid: slots[i] is never larger than the current length of the list. Return the final list.

examples.why: [5] → [6, 5] → [6, 7, 5]. The 7 goes between 6 and 5 because it is inserted, not written over.
The first three append. The last one pushes 2 and 3 right.
Writing nums[i] straight to result[slots[i]] would overwrite the 3 and leave the last place empty. Later inserts move earlier values.

hints: This is a direct simulation. Which list operation inserts at a position and shifts the rest?
JavaScript has splice(index, 0, value); Python has list.insert(index, value).
If you write the shifting yourself: grow the list by one, move elements from the end down to the slot one place right, then write the value.

explain.intuition:
The statement already is the algorithm: keep a list and perform each insert in order. The only trap is to treat slots[i] as a final position and assign result[slots[i]] = nums[i]. Later inserts can push an earlier value further right, so you have to insert and shift, not overwrite. It is exactly what happens when you insert a new item into a rendered list in the DOM: everything after it moves down.

With at most 100 elements, the O(n²) cost of shifting is nothing. For large inputs you would process the inserts backwards with a Fenwick tree that finds the k-th free slot, which is a nice follow-up.
steps: For each i, insert nums[i] at index slots[i] of out, shifting the tail right.
pitfalls: Assigning into a pre-sized array at slots[i]. Values get overwritten instead of shifted.
Shifting from the front of the tail toward the end. That copies one value over the whole tail; shift from the end backwards.
Forgetting that an insert at slots[i] = current length is a plain append.

solutions.title: Built-in insert
solutions.idea: Use the language's insert-at-index operation for each pair in order.

solutions.title: Manual shift
solutions.idea: Grow the list by one, move the tail right one place starting from the end, and write the value into the freed slot.

followups: n grows to 10⁵. Process the inserts from last to first: the last insert's slot is final. How does a Fenwick tree find the k-th still-empty position?
Could a balanced tree with subtree sizes (an order-statistic tree) do it online, in the original order?
lcTitle: Create Target Array in the Given Order
